_comment: Where the 'Life in Bible times' extra (crates/atlas-cli/src/extra_customs.rs) reads James M. Freeman's Hand-Book of Bible Manners and Customs, and what was checked against the printed book, on 2026-11-01.

writer.name: James Midwinter Freeman
writer.about: Methodist minister; from 1872 assistant editor of Sunday-school and tract publications of the Methodist Episcopal Church

read.quote: He entered the Methodist ministry and in 1872 became assistant editor of various Sunday-school and tract publications of the Methodist Episcopal church.

work.title: Hand-Book of Bible Manners and Customs
work.published: New York: Nelson & Phillips; Cincinnati: Hitchcock & Walden, 1874

scan.what: the 1874 printing, scanned by the Library of Congress, 532 pages

work.title_page: HAND-BOOK / OF / Bible Manners and Customs. / BY / Rev. JAMES M. FREEMAN, A.M. / ... / New York : / NELSON & PHILLIPS. / CINCINNATI : HITCHCOCK A WALDEN. / 1874. (OCR of the scan; copyright line: "Entered according to Act of Congress, in the year 1874, by NELSON & PHILLIPS.")
work.not_this_work: The New Manners and Customs of the Bible (1996, revised by Harold J. Chadwick) is a different, copyrighted work and is not used.

copy_used.file: Freeman - Manners and Customs of the Bible.book.zip
copy_used.transcriber: Bible Truth Publishers (bibletruthpublishers.com); the last entry ends: "Courtesy of BibleTruthPublishers.com. Most likely this text has not been proofread."

checked.what: entry 1, Use of the Term Father (Genesis 4:20-21), opening sentence
checked.scan: IN the East the originator of any custom is frequently spoken of as the "father" of that custom; so, also, a man is often described by representing him to be the "father" of some peculiarity which distinguishes him from others.
checked.result: word for word the same as the copy used, apart from the style of quotation marks

its heading verse holds at least 60% of the King James words printed under the heading (a verse either side allowed); 10 entries whose heading verse was misread were placed on the one verse holding at least 90% of those words, 6 entries left out (the build prints both lists)

not_checked: Entries after Genesis 24 were not compared with the scan word for word; the transcription is unproofread, so Greek and Hebrew letters in particular may be misread. The panel at Deep says so.
